It is the escrow's computeChannelId, keccak256(abi.encode(payer, payee, token, salt, authorizedSigner, address(this), block.chainid)) (draft-hedera-session-00 L351-371 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87; contracts/src/HederaStreamChannel.sol L307-314 at tomrowbo/mppx-hedera b5193b42, the reference escrow the draft names). expectChannelId and expectChannelIdH2 are computed with eth-abi 6.0.0's encode and eth-utils 6.0.0's keccak on Python 3.12.3; expectChannelIdH2Prefix and expectChannelIdH2Suffix are expectChannelIdH2's first 4 bytes and last 2.

HS2.case: build(...) with SS1's placed C_H, from fixed.payer and deposit 10000000. calls[0].data is expectApproveCalldata: ERC-20 approve(address,uint256) of the escrow for the deposit, the approval the draft requires before open (draft-hedera-session-00 L441-445 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87) and the reference client sends (packages/mppx-hedera/src/client/session.ts L213-220 at tomrowbo/mppx-hedera b5193b42). calls[1].data is expectOpenCalldata: the escrow's open(address,address,uint128,bytes32,address) (draft L417-439) with SS1's recipient and currency, the deposit, H as the salt and a zero authorizedSigner. Both are encoded with eth-utils 6.0.0's function_signature_to_4byte_selector and eth-abi 6.0.0's encode on Python 3.12.3; the lengths, prefixes, suffix, selector and salt bytes are of them. expectVoucherDigest is the EIP-712 digest of Voucher(bytes32 channelId,uint128 cumulativeAmount) under the domain {name "Hedera Stream Channel", version "1", chainId 296, verifyingContract the escrow}, with HS1's expectChannelId and cumulativeAmount 0 (draft L1068-1142; HederaStreamChannel.sol L26, L36-39 and L367-370), computed with eth-account 0.14.0's encode_typed_data and eth-utils' keccak.. complete({openTx: HS3.txHash, signature}) with the signature 0x22 x 65 gives the credential {challenge, payload: expectOpenPayload}: the draft's open credential (draft-hedera-session-00 L880-903 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87: action "open", channelId, txHash, cumulativeAmount, signature), written by hand with HS1.expectChannelId, the transaction hash, the zero initial voucher's amount "0" and that signature

SV1.case: build's request.salt, the salt of SV2's open: H's first 8 bytes read as a little-endian u64, so the salt's encoded bytes in the open instruction's data are exactly H's first 8 bytes (docs/reference/api/svm.md, sessionSalt; docs/reference/pairings.md, mpp/session/solana). The draft leaves the salt to the client, a u64 written little-endian after the instruction discriminator (draft-solana-session-00 L447 and L455-459 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87). expectSalt and expectSaltHex are computed with @solana/kit 8.4.0's getU64Decoder of H's first 8 bytes, Python 3.12.3's int.from_bytes(H[:8], "little") agreeing by hand; plants.solana.expectSaltH2 is the same of H2.

SV3.case: expectVoucher is solanaVoucher(SV2's channel, 100), and the ed25519-raw message buildWithin writes for a voucher of 100 on SV2's opening: the 50 bytes the draft's voucher signs, 0x56 0x01, the channel's 32 address bytes, cumulativeAmount as a u64 little-endian and expiresAt 0 as an i64 little-endian (draft-solana-session-00 L1419-1429 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87), computed with @solana/kit 8.4.0's getAddressEncoder, getU64Encoder and getI64Encoder, Python 3.12.3 agreeing by hand. expectProofText is sessionProof of SV2's channel, payer and fixed.MV1, the UTF-8 the payer signs in operator mode: the draft's JCS object {channelId, domain "mpp-session-auth-v1", payer, sessionChallengeId} (draft-solana-session-00 L1131-1142, RFC 8785), computed with canonicalize 5.1.0.

SV5.about: Operator mode's opening (draft-solana-session-00, Session Bearer Proof): SS1's C_S with methodDetails.voucherSigner "operator" and methodDetails.operator set (the operator key here is SS1's feePayerKey, as a test value). In operator mode the open instruction's authorizedSigner (account 4) is the challenged operator (draft-solana-session-00 L1252-1254 and L1982-1985 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87), so the channel client answers SV5.opening, not SV2's open, whose account 4 is the payer; the payer (seed 01) then signs SV5.opening.expectProofText as ed25519-raw, and the open payload gains authentication = {type: "proof", challengeId, payer, signature}, the signature in base58. Its hex is SV5.opening.expectProofSignature.

opening.case: An operator-mode open, written by hand in Python 3.12.3 from the Solana v0 message format: SV2's message with the open instruction's account 4 (authorizedSigner) the operator, static key 0, which is also the fee payer and rentPayer; static key 3, the channel, the canonical program-derived address of SV2's channel program over the seeds "channel", payer, payee, mint, authorizedSigner, the salt (u64 little-endian) and openSlot (u64 little-endian), the seeds from which SV2's channel derives with the payer as authorizedSigner (draft-solana-session-00 L378-394 and L471 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87: the authorized signer is a PDA seed); static key 2, the escrow, that channel's associated token account for the mint; every other byte SV2's. The derivation is SHA-256 over the seeds, the bump, the program and "ProgramDerivedAddress", taking the first bump from 255 whose hash is not an Ed25519 point. The payer (seed 01) signs the message with cryptography 41.0.7's Ed25519 in the second signature slot; the fee payer's slot is zero, as in SV2. The same procedure with the payer as account 4 writes SV2's wire byte for byte. expectProofText is the JCS object {channelId, domain "mpp-session-auth-v1", payer, sessionChallengeId} for this channel, the payer and fixed.MV1 (draft-solana-session-00 L1131-1142, RFC 8785), and expectProofSignature the payer's Ed25519 signature of it, both by hand in Python 3.12.3. expectReference.digest is the SHA-256 of the message.

XS1.case: xrplChannelId(account, destination, sequence): the PayChannel ledger entry's ID, the SHA-512Half of the PayChannel space key 0x0078, the source's AccountID, the destination's AccountID and the Sequence of the PaymentChannelCreate (xrpl.org, PayChannel, "PayChannel ID Format": docs/references/protocol/ledger-data/ledger-entry-types/paychannel.md L97-103 at XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal 1a22a493; rippled src/libxrpl/protocol/Indexes.cpp L99, L131-135 and L437-441 and include/xrpl/protocol/digest.h L152-166 and L212-221 at XRPLF/rippled 791c96fa, which hash the space as a big-endian UInt16 and the sequence as a big-endian UInt32). expect is computed by hand from that format: node:crypto's SHA-512 of those 46 bytes, its first 32 bytes, each AccountID from ripple-binary-codec 2.11.0's AccountID type; Python 3.12.3's hashlib with a hand base58 decoding agrees.

XS2.case: XS2's opening: a PaymentChannelCreate from account, the payer of Ed25519 entropy 01x16, to SS1's xrpl recipient, of deposit drops, with settleDelay, fee, sequence and lastLedgerSequence, and one memo whose MemoData is the UTF-8 of toLcpString(H), signed by the payer. expectTxJson is written by hand from xrpl.org's PaymentChannelCreate (docs/references/protocol/transactions/types/paymentchannelcreate.md L38-45) and Transaction Common Fields (docs/references/protocol/transactions/common-fields.md L10-30 and L110-116) at XRPLF/xrpl-dev-portal 1a22a493, with these values. build's request.txJson is expectTxJson, and the blob's fields other than SigningPubKey and TxnSignature, as ripple-binary-codec 2.11.0 decodes them, are expectTxJson. The blob is reproduced byte for byte from expectTxJson: the payer's key is derived from the entropy by xrpl.org's Ed25519 Key Derivation (docs/concepts/accounts/cryptographic-keys.md L162-176, node:crypto's SHA-512Half and @noble/curves 2.4.0), its signature is @noble/curves' Ed25519 over ripple-binary-codec's encodeForSigning, and the blob is ripple-binary-codec's encode with SigningPubKey and TxnSignature. ripple-binary-codec is the peer lcp reads blobs with; build writes txJson without it. expectChannel is XS1's formula for account, SS1's xrpl recipient and sequence, computed by hand as XS1's is.. complete({signedBlob: blob, claimSignature: "C042FD"}) gives the credential {challenge, source, payload: expectOpenPayload}, source did:pkh:xrpl:1:account: the draft's open credential (draft-xrpl-session-00 L336-350 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87: action "open", transaction, amount, signature), written by hand with blob, SS1's xrpl request amount and that claim signature

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

HS6.about: recover and status where the opening names no channel, as a transaction and its challenge reported without the credential do not: reference writes the transaction and the escrow alone, the challenge's methodDetails.escrowContract in lower case (fixed.escrow), and recover reads the one ChannelOpened log from the escrow with four topics and four 32-byte data words, giving its data word 2. Each receipt is read in a block at or below the reader's finalized mark. Row 0 is HS4's live opening receipt, whose one ChannelOpened gives HS4's salt; row 1 adds HS3's ChannelOpened from the same escrow, naming HS1's channel, so two are logged; row 2 is HS4's live close receipt, which logs the escrow's ChannelClosed and no ChannelOpened; row 3 names HS1's channel in a binding log over HS4's opening receipt, whose one ChannelOpened names HS4's channel; row 4 is HS4's opening receipt with status 0 and no logs, as a reverted transaction's receipt holds none. Zero logs, two, or a given channel that no log names is hedera/channel-log-not-found, and a revert hedera/reverted. expectStatus is status's answer for the same ref and receipt: status reads the escrow alone as recover does, so the escrow's one ChannelOpened settles the opening at its block (blockNumber a decimal string), and zero logs or two are failed binding-log-not-found; it reads a binding log by that log, so row 3 is failed binding-log-not-found; a revert is failed reverted.

SV6.about: Openings whose open instruction names its authorizedSigner (account 4) or its channel (account 5) through an address lookup table, read through fetchPresented, which reads each table account at finalized and writes tables: for each lookup in order, the table's address and its entries at the lookup's writable and read-only indexes. bound, reference and buildWithin then read the open's accounts through them (draft-solana-session-00 L1962-1964 at tempoxyz/mpp-specs 08e7dd87). Each table account is the one the address lookup table program (AddressLookupTab1e1111111111111111111111111) wrote in the LiteSVM bundled with solders 0.26.0, made by the authority of Ed25519 seed 09 as its made says; madeAt is the address the program gave it, and a row's reader serves it, at finalized, at the address the row's accounts name (null: no account; owner or dataBytes: the account with that owner, or its data cut to that many bytes). Its data is the program's: a 56-byte header (u32 1, the u64 deactivation slot, the u64 last-extended slot, the u8 start index, the optional authority and two bytes of padding) and 32 bytes per entry (solana-address-lookup-table-interface 3.0.0, state.rs). Each row's expect is fetchPresented's answer, its tables, from @solana/kit 8.4.0's message decoder and the table's entries, or a refusal; bound, channel and signer are what bound, reference's channel and buildWithin's signer give after it. A challenge is client (SS1.solana with voucherSigner client), C_S (SS1.solana.placed) or operator (SS1.solana with voucherSigner operator and operator agreedRefusals.rows[21].operator; its opening carries authentication naming its id), each placed as SS1.solana is. liteSvm is LiteSVM's answer to the opening sent with those accounts, signatures and blockhash unchecked: InvalidProgramForExecution is an opening whose addresses loaded, the payment-channels program being absent there. A row's before, when given, is what bound and reference answer before fetchPresented, svm/read-first otherwise; its read, when given, lists the addresses fetchPresented reads, every address its accounts name otherwise. Before any read, fetchPresented and bound check what needs no account: the one open, its salt, the channelId and authentication, so an opening that fails one gets its code whatever its lookups hold. fetchPresented reads every table before it answers, and a svm/table-unusable in one lookup comes before a read to repeat in another.

no account at the table's address (AddressLookupTableNotFound): svm/not-found, a read to repeat, since a table created in a block that is not finalized is not in the read at finalized

the table account owned by the System program, holding the table's data (InvalidAccountOwner; the address lookup table program cannot create a table over an account that holds data): svm/table-unusable
the table account's data less its last byte, not 56 bytes and whole 32-byte entries (InvalidAccountData): svm/table-unusable

a deactivated table, its deactivation slot set: svm/table-unusable, because the opening may land after the table stops resolving: the runtime loads from it only until that slot leaves SlotHashes, which holds the slots of the last 512 blocks, nothing makes it active again, and a durable nonce keeps an opening valid with no expiry. The table's deactivation slot is 1000, and its liteSvm is LiteSVM's answer at slot 5000, past that cool-down (LookupTableAccountNotFound)

an index past the entries of a table its authority can still extend (InvalidLookupIndex): svm/not-found, a read to repeat, since an entry appended in a block that is not finalized is not in the read at finalized
an index past the entries of a frozen table, which takes no new entry (InvalidLookupIndex): svm/table-unusable

a table entry that repeats a static key, the payer, as the channel (AccountLoadedTwice, agave v3.0.14 accounts-db/src/account_locks.rs L160-170; LiteSVM checks no account locks and runs on to the program): svm/table-unusable
tables that are not, for each lookup in order, its table's address with as many base58 keys as it names writable and read-only indexes, given to bound and reference: svm/read-first
three lookups whose tables hold no account, and no open instruction: svm/open-not-found, from bound and reference without tables and from fetchPresented, which reads no table

three lookups whose tables hold no account, and an open whose salt is another agreement's hash: mpp/carrier-not-challenge, from bound and reference without tables and from fetchPresented, which reads no table

two lookups, the first of a table that holds no account (a read to repeat), the second of a deactivated table (svm/table-unusable): fetchPresented reads both, and the refusal no later read changes comes first, svm/table-unusable

two lookups, the first of a table that holds no account (a read to repeat), the second of a table whose entry repeats a static key, the payer, as the channel (AccountLoadedTwice): fetchPresented reads both, and the repeat among the addresses that resolve comes first, svm/table-unusable

an account the System program owns with no data at the table's address (InvalidAddressLookupTableOwner while it stands): svm/not-found, a read to repeat, since the address lookup table program creates a table at an address the System program holds lamports for (solana-program/address-lookup-table ac994f09, program/src/processor.rs L185-211); in LiteSVM, CreateLookupTable and ExtendLookupTable then succeed at that address and the opening's addresses load (InvalidProgramForExecution)

a lookup that names no index (SanitizeFailure: "each lookup table must be used to load at least one account", anza-xyz/solana-sdk 648387ee message/src/versions/v0/mod.rs L118-129): svm/tx-malformed, from bound and reference and from fetchPresented, which reads no table
